title: Lesson 17: Packaging Reusable Skills: Turning What You Build Once Into Assets You Reuse Everywhere
description: Turning a solved problem into a reusable skill: deciding what deserves packaging, writing it as lessons rather than a log, stripping the client out so it travels, and shipping it where the next engagement can load it.

questions.question: Why should a skill's description name the situation it applies to rather than just its topic?
options: It is displayed to the client as the title of the deliverable
It is the only part loaded when relevance is decided
It determines which model tier the skill's work runs on
It stores the credentials the skill needs at run time
questions.explanation: Only the description is loaded at the moment relevance is decided, so naming the situation earns the skill a chance to load.

questions.question: How should a reusable skill treat the details that belong to a single client?
options: Inline real names and keys so the steps read concretely
Store credentials in the file so the skill is self-contained
Keep secrets out by name and settings in configuration
Fork the skill per client and edit in their specifics
questions.explanation: The transferable procedure stays client-neutral: secrets are referenced by name and client specifics live in configuration, so the asset travels.

questions.question: What belongs in the body of a skill?
options: An ordered procedure with its pitfalls and checks
A narrative of the incident with dates and ticket numbers
A transcript of how the tool first failed during discovery
A list of every client the procedure has been used for
questions.explanation: Skills hold rules rather than logs: a general rule plus a short why, attached to the step it affects and stated once.
